blocking.section: Decision outcome (because-clause); Consequences; Pros and cons of the options (Helm chart and mirrored CRDs, Gateway API deferred)
blocking.issue: The ADR says the Kubernetes API stays off Nodes and that Nodes hold no watch. The owning document and the tech stack document say otherwise. On Kubernetes, Nodes link client-go and hold watches for `discovery: kubernetes` EndpointSlices and for `provider: kubernetes` secrets. So an API server outage does more than stop new CRD changes. It freezes EndpointSlice discovery and Kubernetes secret refresh. A Node restarted during the outage also cannot resolve a `provider: kubernetes` secretRef, and pack 8.5 then keeps it not ready.
blocking.evidence: Line 46: "keeps the Kubernetes API off Nodes and ships with Ruralz Control"; line 115: "Good, because an API server outage stops only new CRD changes: Nodes hold no watch and keep their active Revision (P9)."; line 136: "Good, because Kubernetes stays optional and off Nodes." The owning document docs/operations/01-deployment-topologies.md, T4 RBAC row (line 187), says: "Nodes: `get` and `watch` on own-namespace Secrets, only for `provider: kubernetes`; `list` and `watch` on `endpointslices.discovery.k8s.io`". docs/engineering/01-tech-stack-and-libraries.md line 82 says: "client-go is always linked into `ruralzd` and `ruralz-control`". Pack 8.5: `/readyz` returns 200 only when "every `secretRef` it uses has resolved".
blocking.fix: Line 46: replace "keeps the Kubernetes API off Nodes" with "keeps CRDs and configuration delivery off Nodes". Line 115: "Good, because an API server outage stops new CRD changes, and freezes EndpointSlice discovery and `provider: kubernetes` secret refresh at their last state, while running Nodes keep their active Revision (P9); a Node restarted during the outage stays not ready if it needs a `provider: kubernetes` secret (pack 8.5)." Line 136: "Good, because Kubernetes stays optional and configuration delivery stays off Nodes." In the Figure 1 label, "Nodes: ruralzd, no CRD access" is correct and can stay.

blocking.issue: Figure 2 gives `RefNotFound` as a reason for `Accepted` False. In the Configuration model, which is the only source for the status conditions, `RefNotFound` is a false reason of `ResolvedRefs`. `Accepted` has only `InvalidSpec` and `GuardrailViolation`.
blocking.evidence: Line 101: "C->>A: Accepted False, InvalidSpec or RefNotFound". docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md, Status conditions in the CRD path: "| `Accepted` | Schema and semantic checks pass | `InvalidSpec`, `GuardrailViolation` |" and "| `ResolvedRefs` | Every reference resolves | `RefNotFound`, `PluginDigestMissing` |".
blocking.fix: Change line 101 to "C->>A: Accepted False (InvalidSpec) or ResolvedRefs False (RefNotFound)".

blocking.issue: The Consequences say authors need only namespace-scoped RBAC. The ADR's own CRD translation row, the Configuration model's Kubernetes mapping and the owning document all make `Environment` and `Cluster` cluster-scoped CRDs. Anyone who authors those two kinds needs cluster-scoped RBAC. The owning document also grants `ruralz-control` cluster-scoped CRD status updates, and Migration tooling needs cluster-scoped RBAC on CRD status to prune stored versions.
blocking.evidence: Line 116: "Good, because authors need only namespace-scoped RBAC, and no chart component reads Secrets cluster-wide." Line 52: "`Environment` and `Cluster` are cluster-scoped". docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md, Kubernetes mapping: "| `Environment`, `Cluster` | Outside the Bundle | Cluster-scoped CRDs read only by Ruralz Control |". docs/operations/01-deployment-topologies.md line 187: "reads of cluster-scoped `Environment` and `Cluster` CRDs, cluster-scoped CRD status updates".
blocking.fix: Rewrite line 116 as: "Good, because authors of Bundle kinds need only namespace-scoped RBAC; only platform operators who author the cluster-scoped `Environment` and `Cluster` objects need cluster-scoped rights, and no chart component reads Secrets cluster-wide."

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (Figure 1); CRD versions row; Consequences
non_blocking.suggestion: Figure 1 puts the conversion webhook inside the "Ruralz Control (ruralz-control) leader" subgraph. That suggests only the leader serves it. Line 120 says reads fail only "while every Ruralz Control replica is down", which suggests every replica serves it. Move `conv` out of the leader subgraph, or label it "every replica". Also, with `conversion.strategy: None` the API server never calls the webhook. Say that the webhook ships unused until a second version is served, Planned (M3).

Line 51 cites OQ-configuration-model-3 (a) for "`rz` plus the lower-case kind, except `rzgw` and `rzenv`". The Configuration model states option (a) as only "`rzgw`, `rzcluster`". The ADR matches the owning document's decision, but it should add a Proposed amendment in More information asking the Configuration model to record the full short-name rule when it closes OQ-configuration-model-3.

OQ-system-overview-8 option (a) reads "One source per Cluster". The ADR, like the owning document, decides one primary source per Environment. Say briefly that the Environment is the unit because every Cluster in it shares one Revision (pack 8.1), so readers do not see a mismatch with the OQ wording.

The URL https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/client-go/informers/discovery/v1 documents EndpointSlice informers, not CRD watches. Rephrase so the citation backs only the per-kind list-and-watch cost, or say that CRDs would need dynamic or generated informers.

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (CRD translation row); Confirmation (Equivalence test)
non_blocking.suggestion: The canonical form keeps labels and annotations in the digest; it drops only comments and file names. "Only the group changes" also needs the translation to drop server-populated metadata (`namespace`, `uid`, `resourceVersion`, `managedFields`) and `status`, and to decide what happens to tool annotations such as `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration`. Otherwise the Equivalence test's MUST cannot hold. Coordinate the fix with L1-3.

The Upgrade test has no milestone tag and no owning test section. Tag it Planned (M3), since it only has meaning once `ruralz.io/v1beta1` is served, and mark it (proposed) like the Equivalence test. Also write "kind (Kubernetes in Docker)" once, so the tool is not confused with a Ruralz resource kind.

There are no FAIL lines. Six WARN milestone lines (52, 54, 55, 125, 126 and 127) have no matching M2 item because the roadmap does not exist yet. When the roadmap is written, make sure its M2 section lists the CRD translation, CRD source, CRD versions, the CRD drift gate, the Equivalence test and the kind suite.
The prose body, excluding fenced blocks, is about 1,330 words against the 1,500 maximum. The L1 and L2 fixes fit in the remaining space. Do not remove text that resolved earlier findings.
